messages:
anya-platform: Heads-up — prototyping a scoped config lifecycle for runtime feature flags and per-scope overrides (route/model/customer). Want quick feedback on API shape, telemetry hooks, and Console UX before I file an RFC.

sam-runtime: 👍 paste the expected API payload + runtime invariants?

anya-platform: Rough draft payload: 

POST /api/v1/configs/apply
{
  "scope": { "type": "route", "id": "generate-text-v2" },
  "config": { "batching": { "max_tokens": 1024 }, "qos": "latency-priority" },
  "phase": "canary",
  "canary": { "cohort_count": 1000, "cohort_size": 1 },
  "dry_run": true,
  "safety_budget": { "p99_ms_delta": 35, "error_rate_delta_pct": 0.25 },
  "meta": { "author": "anya-platform", "reason": "reduce p99 for long prompts" }
}

(we're preferring cohort-based routing for determinism)
messages_more:
sam-runtime: A couple constraints: async/nonblocking apply, worker should return change_id + etag for optimistic concurrency. Dry-run must simulate kernel selection and memory. Cohort routing needs consistent hashing so sessions stay sticky.

jorge-sre: Telemetry requirements: pre/post buckets for p50/p95/p99, error_rate (5xx + rate-limited), queue_length. Canary emits hourly snapshots and a verdict event: config.canary.v1.{change_id}.verdict = {pass|fail|inconclusive}. Also a sampled eval: run ~100 prompts through canary vs baseline to surface functional drift.

liz-devex: Console flow proposal: Draft -> Dry Run (auto-generate simulated latency histograms) -> Submit for Approval (optional approval list) -> Canary -> Monitor -> Promote/Rollback. Show one-line diff, estimated qps/mem impact, and a small histogram in the dry-run. Approvals should integrate with Slack (config-approvals channel) and include approve/reject actions.

sam-runtime: API notes: return {change_id, etag, dry_run_report_url}, store attempted node list and rollback plan. State machine: DRAFT -> APPLYING -> CANARY -> MONITORING -> PROMOTE/ROLLBACK. Abort if X nodes fail to apply in Y seconds. Also add immediate short-circuit rollback triggers for severe regressions.

anya-platform: Important: idempotent applies, preflight validation (schema + runtime sim), telemetry gating to auto-abort. Add audit snapshots on every apply (who, git-ref, previous config). Prevent accidental widening of scope (require explicit confirm when moving from route -> org). Precedence order: customer > route > org default.

jorge-sre: Safeguards: if telemetry ingestion for the canary window is delayed >15m, pause the canary and notify leads. Canary window aggregates retained for 90 days; raw traces 7 days. Provide an export hook (S3) when retain_raw=true. Also include an immediate_rollback threshold: p99 multiplier > 2 or error_rate > 5% absolute.

liz-devex: UX rollback: one-click rollback to last change_id. Console should show affected nodes and the metric that triggered the rollback. For approvals Slack messages, attach quick-action buttons (Approve / Reject / Inspect).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config apply request received: change_id=chg_2026_001, dry_run=true, scope=route/generate-text-v2

sam-runtime: Dry-run report must include simulated kernel & memory footprint. If GPU memory would be exceeded, fail the dry-run early. Also report estimated token throughput change.

anya-platform: We'll attach safety_budget to the main API. Example: "safety_budget": { "p99_ms_delta": 35, "error_rate_delta_pct": 0.25 } and short-circuit thresholds as Jorge suggested.

jorge-sre: Also include a canary verdict event and hourly snapshots so Alerting can subscribe. Make verdict determinable by both rule thresholds and the sampled eval output (functional regression trumps perf improve).

sam-runtime: Question for the group: cohort-based vs percent-based canaries? Cohort-based is better for deterministic tracing, but percent is easier to think about. Thoughts?

anya-platform: Leaning cohort-based for reproducibility and easier trace back to customers; percent-based remains an option for pure load experiments.

jorge-sre: Cohort mapping also helps identify impacted customers for direct outreach.

liz-devex: Action items: Anya to formalize payload + edge cases (etag, change_id, safety_budget); Sam to draft runtime state machine + rollback plan; Jorge to propose telemetry schema & alert thresholds; Liz to wireframe dry-run + approvals + rollback UI. I'll schedule 30m follow-up after RFC draft.

anya-platform: Thanks — will update RFC draft and ping channel. ✨

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: automated note — draft chg_2026_001 saved to drafts/configs/chg_2026_001

sam-runtime: One more: ensure dry_run_report includes simulated kernel memory footprints and per-node allocation.

jorge-sre: And add a fast auto-rollback if the canary shows catastrophic spikes (15m auto rollback). We shouldn't wait the full window for severe regressions.

anya-platform: Adding short-circuit thresholds and the abort-on-telemetry-lag rule. RFC incoming.

liz-devex: Nice, thanks. I'll post a meeting invite once RFC link is up. :raised_hands:
